stories.headline: Google DeepMind publishes cognitive taxonomy for measuring AGI progress, launches $200K Kaggle hackathon

key_facts.fact: On March 17, Google DeepMind released the paper 'Measuring Progress Toward AGI: A Cognitive Taxonomy' introducing a framework that deconstructs general intelligence into 10 key cognitive faculties drawn from decades of research in psychology, neuroscience, and cognitive science.
key_facts.excerpt: We present a framework for understanding system capabilities in relation to human cognitive abilities. Drawing from decades of research in psychology, neuroscience, and cognitive science, we introduce a Cognitive Taxonomy that deconstructs general intelligence into 10 key cognitive faculties.

key_facts.fact: The framework proposes a rigorous evaluation protocol generating a 'cognitive profile' for AI systems—measuring performance across a suite of targeted, held-out cognitive tasks to understand a system's strengths and weaknesses, rather than relying on single aggregate scores.
key_facts.excerpt: We then propose a rigorous evaluation protocol in which a system's performance is measured across a suite of targeted, held-out cognitive tasks, generating a 'cognitive profile' that can be used to understand a system's strengths and weaknesses.

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind launched a Kaggle hackathon with a $200,000 prize pool inviting the community to design evaluations for key cognitive abilities identified in the taxonomy.
key_facts.excerpt: We're introducing a framework to measure progress toward AGI, and launching a Kaggle hackathon to build the relevant evaluations.

key_facts.fact: The paper was authored by a team including Ryan Burnell, Meredith Ringel Morris, Allan Dafoe, Noah D. Goodman, Matthew Botvinick, and Shane Legg, building on DeepMind's earlier 'Levels of AGI' framework published at ICML 2024.
key_facts.excerpt: Ryan Burnell, Yumeya Yamamori, Orhan Firat, Kate Olszewska, Steph Hughes-Fitt, Oran Kelly, Isaac R. Galatzer-Levy, Meredith Ringel Morris, Allan Dafoe, Alison M. Snyder, Noah D. Goodman, Matthew Botvinick and Shane Legg.

stories.headline: Moonshot AI's Kimi team proposes Attention Residuals, a drop-in fix for transformer depth scaling

key_facts.fact: Moonshot AI's Kimi team published a paper introducing Attention Residuals (AttnRes), which replaces fixed residual connections in transformers with softmax attention over preceding layer outputs, allowing each layer to selectively aggregate earlier representations with learned, input-dependent weights.
key_facts.excerpt: We propose Attention Residuals (AttnRes), which replaces this fixed accumulation with softmax attention over preceding layer outputs, allowing each layer to selectively aggregate earlier representations with learned, input-dependent weights.

key_facts.fact: Block AttnRes, the practical variant, partitions layers into blocks and attends over block-level representations, serving as a drop-in replacement for standard residual connections with minimal overhead while solving the PreNorm dilution problem where uniform aggregation progressively dilutes each layer's contribution.
key_facts.excerpt: We introduce Block AttnRes, which partitions layers into blocks and attends over block-level representations, reducing the memory footprint while preserving most of the gains of full AttnRes.

key_facts.fact: AttnRes was integrated into the Kimi Linear architecture (48B total / 3B activated parameters) and pre-trained on 1.4T tokens, yielding more uniform output magnitudes and gradient distribution across depth, with scaling experiments showing a 1.25x compute-equivalent improvement.
key_facts.excerpt: We further integrate AttnRes into the Kimi Linear architecture (48B total / 3B activated parameters) and pre-train on 1.4T tokens, where AttnRes mitigates PreNorm dilution, yielding more uniform output magnitudes and gradient distribution across depth.

key_facts.fact: The approach draws an analogy between the time dimension (handled by attention) and the depth dimension (handled by residual connections), applying the same selective aggregation principle that made attention successful to the depth axis of transformers.
key_facts.excerpt: Moonshot AI's Kimi team introduced Attention Residuals, a new architecture concept for Transformer models... treating model depth somewhat like a sequence dimension.

stories.headline: UNM and Los Alamos build THOR, an AI framework solving century-old physics calculations 400x faster

key_facts.fact: Researchers at the University of New Mexico and Los Alamos National Laboratory published THOR (Tensors for High-dimensional Object Representation), an AI framework that directly calculates configurational integrals—equations central to statistical mechanics that describe how particles interact within materials—over 400 times faster than conventional supercomputer methods.
key_facts.excerpt: UNM and Los Alamos researchers built an AI system that solves complex atomic interaction calculations in seconds instead of weeks. Their THOR framework runs over 400 times faster than conventional methods while matching supercomputer accuracy.

key_facts.fact: The framework combines tensor network algorithms with machine learning models using 'tensor train cross interpolation' to compress high-dimensional data, and identifies crystal symmetries to further reduce computational demands, solving the 'curse of dimensionality' that made direct calculation impractical for nearly a century.
key_facts.excerpt: The system combines tensor network algorithms with machine learning models using a technique called tensor train cross interpolation to compress multidimensional data.

key_facts.fact: THOR was validated on copper, crystalline argon under extreme pressure, and tin during phase transitions, all matching results from advanced Los Alamos simulations. The work was published in Physical Review Materials.
key_facts.excerpt: The researchers applied THOR AI to copper, crystalline argon under high pressure, and phase transitions in tin—all yielding results matching advanced Los Alamos simulations. The study was published in the journal Physical Review Materials.

key_facts.fact: The code is open-sourced on GitHub, enabling other research teams to apply the methodology. Calculations that previously required weeks of supercomputer time now complete in seconds.
key_facts.excerpt: Calculations that previously required weeks of supercomputer time now complete in seconds. The code is accessible on GitHub.

stories.headline: Iran war threatens global chip supply as Strait of Hormuz blockade enters third week

key_facts.fact: The US-Iran conflict and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz since March 4, 2026 is threatening the global semiconductor industry, as Taiwan — which manufactures roughly 90% of the world's most advanced chips through TSMC — relies on imported energy flowing through the strait.
key_facts.excerpt: Taiwan, which manufactures roughly 90% of the world's most advanced semiconductors through TSMC alone, runs on imported energy, and a significant chunk of that energy flows through the Strait.

key_facts.fact: The Middle East supplies 37% of the fuel powering Taiwan's electric grid via LNG imports. Qatar, Iran's maritime neighbor, accounts for about one-third of the world's helium supply, which Taiwan imports and is essential for semiconductor production with no viable alternatives.
key_facts.excerpt: The Middle East supplies 37% of the fuel that powers Taiwan's electric grid... Qatar accounts for about one-third of the world's helium supply... Helium is essential for heat management during semiconductor production.

key_facts.fact: TSMC shares have fallen about 7% since the war began, versus a roughly 6% decline in global stocks. TSMC stated it 'does not anticipate any significant impact currently' and will continue monitoring the situation.
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC shares have fallen about 7% since the war began... TSMC said it does not anticipate any significant impact currently.

key_facts.fact: South Korea has warned the conflict could disrupt supply of key chipmaking materials, as the semiconductor industry faces mounting threats that the conflict will choke off key supplies and spike power costs in Taiwan.
key_facts.excerpt: The global semiconductor industry is facing mounting threats the U.S.-Iran conflict will choke off key supplies vital for chipmaking and spike the cost of power in Taiwan.

stories.headline: Trump's counterterrorism chief Joe Kent resigns over Iran war, says it 'posed no imminent threat'

key_facts.fact: National Counterterrorism Center Director Joe Kent announced his resignation on March 17, becoming the highest-ranking Trump administration official to publicly break with the president over the Iran war.
key_facts.excerpt: He is the highest-ranking Trump administration official to announce his resignation over the Iran war.

key_facts.fact: In his resignation letter posted on X, Kent wrote: 'I cannot in good conscience support the ongoing war in Iran. Iran posed no imminent threat to our nation, and it is clear that we started this war due to pressure from Israel and its powerful American lobby.'
key_facts.excerpt: Joe Kent, an Army veteran who completed 11 combat deployments to the Mideast and elsewhere, said he 'cannot in good conscience' support the war.

key_facts.fact: Kent is a decorated Army veteran with 11 combat deployments and a long-time Trump supporter who ran two unsuccessful congressional bids in Washington state as a Republican.
key_facts.excerpt: Joe Kent, an Army veteran who completed 11 combat deployments to the Mideast and elsewhere.

key_facts.fact: Trump dismissed the resignation in the Oval Office, saying Kent was a 'nice guy' but 'weak on security,' adding that the letter made him realize 'it was a good thing that he's out.'
key_facts.excerpt: Trump said Kent was a 'nice guy', but 'weak on security'. He also said Kent's resignation letter had made him realise 'it was a good thing that he's out'.

key_facts.fact: The White House disputed Kent's claims, saying the president had 'compelling evidence' that Iran was going to attack the US first. A US hate monitor accused Kent of employing 'antisemitic tropes.'
key_facts.excerpt: The White House dismissed the letter, saying the president had 'compelling evidence' that Iran was going to attack the US first. A US hate monitor accused Kent of 'antisemitic tropes'.

stories.headline: UK and Ukraine sign defense pact focused on drone warfare and joint production as Zelenskyy visits London

key_facts.fact: UK PM Keir Starmer and Ukrainian President Zelenskyy signed the Enhanced Security and Defence Industrial Collaboration Declaration on March 17, establishing a new defense partnership focused on countering drone threats.
key_facts.excerpt: We, the President of Ukraine and the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom... Meeting in a spirit of unity, shared responsibility, and strategic partnership.

key_facts.fact: The pact includes licensed production of Ukraine's Octopus interceptor drone in the UK and acceleration of the Lyra programme covering drones, air defence, and long-range effectors.
key_facts.excerpt: Licensed production of Ukraine's Octopus interceptor drone in the United Kingdom... accelerating the implementation of the Lyra programme, a portfolio of co-development projects covering drones, air defence, long-range effectors.

key_facts.fact: Starmer said: 'The Middle East conflict has increased the need for rapid military innovation. It's central to our national and economic security.' NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte joined the Downing Street talks.
key_facts.excerpt: The Middle East conflict has increased the need for rapid military innovation. It's central to our national and economic security.

key_facts.fact: Zelenskyy addressed around 120 UK parliamentarians at Westminster, calling Iran and Russia 'brothers in hatred' and warning about the dangers of drone warfare and Iranian Shahed drones sold to Moscow.
key_facts.excerpt: The Iranian and Russian regimes are 'brothers in hatred', Volodymyr Zelensky has told MPs and peers, as he warned about the dangers of drone warfare.

key_facts.fact: Britain and Ukraine also agreed to work together to sell drone technology abroad, combining Ukraine's battlefield experience with British industrial capacity.

stories.headline: SEC and CFTC issue joint token taxonomy declaring most crypto assets are not securities

key_facts.fact: On March 17, the SEC issued a token taxonomy establishing four categories of crypto assets that are not securities: digital commodities, digital collectibles, digital tools, and payment stablecoins under the GENIUS Act.
key_facts.excerpt: Our interpretation establishes four asset categories that are not deemed securities: digital commodities, digital collectibles, digital tools, and payment stablecoins under the GENIUS Act.

key_facts.fact: The CFTC joined the SEC in issuing the interpretation, committing to administer the Commodity Exchange Act consistently with the SEC's guidance. CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said: 'The wait is over.'
key_facts.excerpt: CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig: 'For far too long, American builders, innovators, and entrepreneurs have awaited clear guidance on the status of crypto assets under the federal securities and commodity laws. With today's interpretation, the wait is over.'

key_facts.fact: SEC Chairman Paul Atkins announced the interpretation at the DC Blockchain Summit, saying it 'acknowledges what the former administration refused to recognize — that most crypto assets are not securities.'
key_facts.excerpt: After more than a decade of uncertainty, this interpretation will provide market participants with a clear understanding of how the Commission treats crypto assets under federal securities laws.

key_facts.fact: The guidance also clarifies how federal securities laws apply to protocol mining, staking, and crypto airdrops, and defines when a token transitions from security to commodity status.
key_facts.excerpt: The guidance carves out payment stablecoins, digital collectives and digital commodities as non-securities. It also clarifies how federal securities laws apply to protocol mining, staking and crypto airdrops.

stories.headline: VIX surges 70% YTD as Iran war drives Brent crude past $98 and Strait of Hormuz shipping collapses

key_facts.fact: The CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) surged over 70% year-to-date as of March 17, peaking near the 30-point threshold, driven by the US-Iran conflict escalation.
key_facts.excerpt: The CBOE Volatility Index, better known as the VIX, has skyrocketed by over 70% year-to-date, reflecting a market gripped by uncertainty.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude experienced a 6.9% single-day surge on March 12, reaching $98.30 per barrel, after Iranian forces declared the Strait of Hormuz closed to 'enemy' vessels. Brent has since surged to nearly $120/barrel.
key_facts.excerpt: A 65 percent surge in Brent crude to nearly $120 a barrel as U.S.-led strikes threatened global energy supplies.

key_facts.fact: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which carries approximately 20% of the world's daily oil supply, has fallen to 97% below normal levels.
key_facts.excerpt: Shipping through Strait estimated at 97% below normal levels... approximately 20% of the world's daily oil supply flows.

key_facts.fact: The S&P 500 is down 4.2% since the war began on February 28. Energy stocks rose 1.4-3.3%, defense stocks gained 3-6%, while airlines fell 3-6%.
key_facts.excerpt: The Morningstar US Market Index is down less than 1.6% this week and 4.2% since the war began.

key_facts.fact: Analysts warn the Hormuz blockade could add 0.8% to global inflation by end of 2026, threatening to derail the global disinflationary trend.
key_facts.excerpt: Blockade could add 0.8% to global inflation by end of 2026... threatens to 'derail the global disinflationary trend'.

stories.headline: Nvidia resumes H200 chip manufacturing for China after receiving both US and Beijing approval

key_facts.fact: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang confirmed at GTC 2026 on March 17 that the company has received purchase orders from 'many' Chinese customers and is restarting H200 manufacturing after obtaining approvals from both US and Chinese authorities.
key_facts.excerpt: We've been licensed for many customers in China for H200. We have received purchase orders from many customers and we are in the process of restarting our manufacturing.

key_facts.fact: Beijing's approval to allow H200 imports had been the main barrier to resuming sales. China once accounted for at least 20% of Nvidia's data center revenue, a key market lost during US-China tech tensions.
key_facts.excerpt: Previously, NVIDIA had effectively halted H200 production, repurposing its production lines for next-generation AI chips, citing a lack of purchase orders from Chinese clients.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia is also preparing a version of its Groq inference chip that can be sold to the Chinese market, according to sources familiar with the matter.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia is also preparing a version of the Groq AI chip that can be sold to the Chinese market.

key_facts.fact: The restart comes weeks after CFO Colette Kress warned investors that Nvidia's Q1 2027 revenue forecast didn't account for any revenue from Chinese datacenter customers.
key_facts.excerpt: Huang's comments come just weeks after CFO Colette Kress warned investors that its Q1 2027 revenue forecast didn't account for a single cent of revenue from Chinese datacenter customers.

stories.headline: OpenAI signs Pentagon deal through AWS for classified military AI, replacing Anthropic

key_facts.fact: OpenAI signed a deal on March 17 to sell access to its AI models to US defense and government agencies through Amazon Web Services for both classified and unclassified work.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI has signed a new deal to sell access to its AI models to U.S. defence and government agencies through Amazon's cloud unit for classified and unclassified work.

key_facts.fact: The contract enables OpenAI to support the Pentagon under a deal it secured after the agency dropped Anthropic, which had a contract worth up to $200 million signed in July 2025 with Palantir and AWS.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic, which won a Pentagon contract worth up to US$200-million in July, 2025, had been a key U.S. defence AI supplier, working with Palantir and Amazon Web Services to deploy its Claude models in classified military and intelligence systems.

key_facts.fact: MIT Technology Review reported the Pentagon is also planning secure environments for AI companies to train military-specific model versions on classified data, a new development beyond current use of AI to query classified databases.
key_facts.excerpt: The Pentagon is discussing plans to set up secure environments for generative AI companies to train military-specific versions of their models on classified data.

key_facts.fact: AI models like Anthropic's Claude were already used to analyze targets in Iran. The Pentagon has reached agreements with OpenAI and Elon Musk's xAI to operate their models in classified settings.

stories.headline: PerturbAI launches from stealth with world's largest 8M-cell in vivo CRISPR atlas of brain tissue

key_facts.fact: PerturbAI emerged from stealth on March 17 with the public release of the world's largest in vivo CRISPR atlas: an 8 million-cell, brain-wide dataset mapping gene function directly in living tissue.
key_facts.excerpt: PerturbAI, an AI-native therapeutics company accelerating drug discovery through systems-level understanding of diseases, emerged from stealth today with the public release of the world's largest in vivo CRISPR atlas.

key_facts.fact: The atlas was generated in collaboration with NVIDIA, Allen Institute for Brain Science, and 10x Genomics, mapping the effects of nearly 2,000 disease-linked genes across hundreds of neuronal cell types.
key_facts.excerpt: The in vivo CRISPR atlas was created in collaboration with 10x Genomics, NVIDIA, and the Allen Institute for Brain Science... Its dataset spans 8 million cells.

key_facts.fact: Co-founder Xin Jin said: 'For the first time, we can measure gene function directly inside intact biological systems at a massive scale. This enables systems-level understanding of disease.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'The public release of this CRISPR atlas marks a foundational change for biology,' said Xin Jin, Ph.D., co-founder of PerturbAI.

key_facts.fact: Unlike traditional in vitro systems, PerturbAI's platform measures gene function within intact organs, capturing biological circuitry. The company closed an oversubscribed pre-seed round in Q3 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Unlike traditional in vitro or single-organ systems, PerturbAI's in vivo CRISPR platform measures gene function within intact organs... the startup also emerged from stealth mode, disclosing that it closed an oversubscribed pre-seed round.

stories.headline: London-based Ternary Therapeutics raises $4.4M to develop AI-designed drugs targeting inflammaging

key_facts.fact: London-based Ternary Therapeutics raised $4.4 million (EUR 4.1 million) in a seed round led by Paris-based VC daphni, alongside Pace Ventures, i&i Biotech Fund, and Future Planet Capital.
key_facts.excerpt: London-based Ternary Therapeutics has raised $4.4 million (€4.1 million) in a seed round led by Paris-based VC daphni, alongside Pace Ventures, i&i Biotech Fund and Future Planet Capital.

key_facts.fact: The company is developing AI-designed 'molecular glues' to tame chronic inflammation (inflammaging), a key mechanism in age-related disease and a growing target in longevity medicine.
key_facts.excerpt: Ternary Therapeutics bets AI-designed 'molecular glues' can tame chronic inflammation, opening new doors for longevity medicine.

key_facts.fact: The investment signals selective confidence in a biotech climate where inflammaging is considered one of the trickiest problems in drug discovery.
key_facts.excerpt: On paper, a $4.4 million seed may seem modest, but in today's biotech climate, it is more like a mark of selective confidence. Investors are willing to back a company that promises to tackle one of the trickiest problems in drug discovery.
